text:
sam: CI perf alert on PR #18055 — microbench `batch_latency_us` jumped ~28% on the post-merge CI run. link: https://ci.internal.redwood/78765/builds/18055/output

ci-bot: Threshold diff detected for test `microbench/batch_latency` (baseline=12.3us, head=15.8us). Marking as FAIL.

sam: repro job attached above. looks like KV cache hitrate dipped on the same run (see stats in the build logs). can someone take a quick look? this is blocking the canary rollout. :eyes:

mira: ack. grabbing bisect. will try narrow down to the merge window.

alex: quick skim of the bench output — kernel autoselect picked `cuda_kernel_v2` on head whereas baseline used `cuda_kernel_v1`. timing table: v1 median 11.9us, v2 median 16.2us.

liam: that kernel switch can happen when seq_len distribution shifts. any chance the regression is from synthetic seqlen sampling change in #17988?

jc: also saw increased KV cache miss rate in the logs: prefix_hits dropped 18% for short sequences. suspect interaction between sampler + new batching heuristics.

mira: bisect update: narrowed to merge range 18010..18055. reproduces locally with `bazel run //bench:microbench -- --test=batch_latency --runs=500`.

sam: paste of local reproducer command (for reference):
```
# run microbench locally
python tools/run_microbench.py --bench batch_latency --model redwood-legacy --iters 500 --seed 42
```

alex: I ran the reproducer with perf counters. flame snippet: `hotspots: 42% kernel_dispatch, 25% kv_lookup_miss, 10% memcpy` — kernel dispatch increased due to falling back to v2 which has higher overhead.

liam: confirmed: the kernel selector cost model updated in #18022 to prefer v2 for small batched requests when estimated tensor layout matches a new stride heuristic. looks like the heuristic misclassifies some workloads with the new sampler distribution.

jc: short-term mitigation: force selector to prefer v1 for commit range > 18010 and < 18060, or add a canary gate in the autotuner.

mira: will try a quick revert PR for #18022 (selector change) to see if perf recovers. if revert fixes CI we can do a targeted fix later.

oncall-bot: Revert PR submitted: #18060 by mira — "revert: kernel selector heuristic tweak". CI queued.

sam: thanks. while that runs, can we add a golden microbench test that checks kernel selection invariant for short sequences? we shouldn't rely on sampling randomness in CI.

alex: good idea. propose adding deterministic seqlen buckets and assert selector chooses v1 for the small-batch case. also raise threshold tolerance for batching latency by 15% while we stabilize.

liam: note — raising threshold is dangerous long-term but ok as a temporary unblock. also file follow-up to tighten after autotuner fix.

jc: running deeper profile now to capture KV eviction timing — will post diffs in this thread within the hour.

mira: CI revert PR passed on all microbenches, batch_latency back to baseline (12.1us). canary hold lifted. :thumbsup:

sam: awesome — rolling back the merge for the release. created issue track: https://tracker.internal.redwood/issue/793 "kernel-selector: misclassify small-batch workload with new stride heuristic" — assigning to liam + alex.

alex: quick note — root cause summary for the issue: selector cost model had a tightened memcopy amortization term that assumed contiguous packing; new sampler introduced edge cases where padding caused a fallback to a slower kernel. fix plan: refine packing check and add unit test for sampler/kselector interaction.

liam: I'll own the fix. plan: revert is temporary, will land targeted patch + tests next week.

sam: thanks all. follow-ups: jc to upload full perf flamegraphs and kv traces to the issue, alex to add golden microbench, liam implements fix. leaving thread open for traces.

jc: uploaded artifacts: https://ci.internal.redwood/artifacts/18055/perf.tar.gz (flamegraphs + kv-trace).

mira: closing the immediate rollout blocker — moving to postmortem/issue tracking.

sam: great work.
